title: He knows now: this is the parting.
subtitle: The certainty of leaving everything
then: After the search for a cure fails, the dying man {trap}is certain it is the time of separation.{/trap} Ibn Kathir describes this as the moment death's terrors are seen. {idea}What he doubted in health, he is sure of now.{/idea}
now: You hold your grandmother's hand in the last week. She stops asking about the house and the money. She asks who will visit. {idea}At the parting, people see clearly what mattered.{/idea}
old: I will always have more time with the people and things I love.
new: Every bond here has a parting. I want to use the time well.
try: Tell one person you love something you would regret not saying.

title: Leg wound around leg: hardship meets hardship.
subtitle: The last day here, the first day there
then: Ibn Abbas said it is {trap}the last day of this world and the first of the Hereafter: hardship meeting hardship{/trap}, {reward}except for whom Allah has mercy on.{/reward} Al-Hasan said it is the two shins bound together, the legs that once carried him now still.
now: You walk all day without a thought: to the bus, up the stairs, to the fridge. Your legs feel like they will always carry you. {idea}One day they will be still, and you will be carried.{/idea} Where are they taking you now?
old: My body will keep carrying me where I want to go.
new: My legs are on loan. I want them to have walked to good places.
try: Walk somewhere good today: the mosque, a visit, an errand for someone else.

title: That Day, the drive is toward your Lord.
subtitle: The soul is taken back
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the place of return and the destination.{/idea} He cites the verse where Allah's messengers take the soul and {idea}they are returned to Allah, their true Master.{/idea} Verse 12 said the same about the Day of Resurrection; here it is about every death.
now: People say "rest in peace" and "they are in a better place" without thinking. {idea}The surah says exactly where they went: to their Lord.{/idea} That is also where you are going.
new: Death is a journey that ends in front of my Lord.
try: Say Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un once today and think about its meaning.

title: He did not believe, and he did not pray.
subtitle: No good inside, no good outside
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the man {trap}who denied the truth in his heart and turned away from acting on it.{/trap} So {trap}there is no good in him, inside or outside.{/trap} After the scene of death, the surah shows the life that led there.
now: You tell yourself your heart is fine, so the prayers can wait. Or you pray on autopilot while your heart is somewhere else. {idea}The verse pairs the two: belief inside, prayer outside.{/idea}
old: As long as my heart is good, the outward acts do not matter much.
new: Belief and prayer go together. Each keeps the other alive.
try: Pray your next prayer with one moment of real attention in it.

title: Instead, he called it a lie and turned away.
subtitle: The two steps of rejection
then: The verse mirrors the one before: {trap}not believing became denying; not praying became turning away.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says he denied in his heart and {trap}turned from acting on its way.{/trap}
now: Someone sends you a reminder. First you think: that is extreme. Then you mute the chat. {idea}Deny, then turn away. Two small moves that shape a whole life.{/idea}
old: Ignoring a reminder is harmless. I am not attacking anyone.
new: Turning away is a choice, and it follows close behind denial.
try: The next reminder you get today, read it fully instead of scrolling past.

title: Then he strutted home, pleased with himself.
subtitle: Arrogance after rejecting the truth
then: Ibn Abbas said it means {trap}arrogantly{/trap}; Qatadah said {trap}strutting.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse about one who {trap}was joyful among his people, thinking he would never come back{/trap}, but {idea}his Lord was ever watching him.{/idea}
now: You win the argument in the family chat by being sharp, not by being right. You put the phone down feeling great. {idea}Feeling pleased with yourself is not the same as being right.{/idea}
old: If I walk away feeling good, I must have handled it well.
new: A proud walk after turning from the truth is the worst kind of win.
try: Think of one argument you won unfairly and send a softer message.

title: Woe to you, and woe.
subtitle: A warning that answers the strut
then: Ibn Abbas reported that {idea}the Prophet ﷺ said this to Abu Jahl, then Allah revealed it.{/idea} Qatadah said Abu Jahl replied that he was {trap}the mightiest man walking between Makkah's two mountains.{/trap}
now: You have a moment of power: the bigger title, the louder voice, the one everyone is afraid to correct. It feels like nothing can touch you. {idea}That is exactly the feeling this warning answers.{/idea}
old: When I am strong, warnings do not apply to me.
new: The stronger I feel, the more I need to hear warnings.
try: Ask someone you trust to tell you one thing you do that comes across as arrogant.

title: Then again: woe to you, and woe.
subtitle: A threat followed by a threat
then: Qatadah said: {trap}it is a threat followed by a threat, just as you hear it.{/trap} Ibn Kathir compares it to the line "eat and enjoy yourselves for a little." {idea}The repetition is there because the first was brushed off.{/idea}
now: The warning light in your car comes on. You ignore it. A week later it flashes and beeps. {idea}Repeated warnings are a mercy. They mean you still have time.{/idea}
old: If a warning repeats, it is just nagging.
new: A repeated warning is a second chance I have not used yet.
try: Name one warning you have heard more than once, from a doctor, a friend, your own heart, and act on it.

title: Do you think you will be left to drift?
subtitle: Not unguided here, not forgotten after

row.title: after death
sub: raised, not left in the grave

then: As-Suddi said it means {trap}not resurrected{/trap}; Mujahid and Ash-Shafi'i said {trap}not commanded and forbidden.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the verse includes both: {idea}man is guided in this life and gathered back to Allah after it.{/idea}
now: Some days feel like drift: wake, work, scroll, sleep. Nothing seems to matter much. {idea}The verse says your days are not empty. They have instructions, and they have a return.{/idea}
old: My life is mine to drift through however I like.
new: My life has a purpose here and an account after. It matters.
try: Write down one thing you are sure Allah wants from you, and do a piece of it today.

title: You started as a tiny drop.
subtitle: The first creation as proof of the second
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}uses the beginning of creation as proof for its repetition.{/idea} Was man not {trap}a weak drop of a lowly fluid{/trap}? The doubter of resurrection is reminded of his own start.
now: You feel big: your degree, your car, your opinions. You argue about what Allah can and cannot do. {idea}You were once a drop no one could see.{/idea}
old: I am too complex to be made again from nothing.
new: I was made from almost nothing once. That is the proof.
try: When you feel proud today, remember the drop. Say Alhamdulillah.

title: Then a clot, then shaped and balanced.
subtitle: Each stage by His design
then: Ibn Kathir describes it: {idea}a clot, then a lump of flesh, then formed, and the soul was blown into him.{/idea} Then he became {reward}a complete creation with healthy limbs.{/reward}
now: Someone shares an ultrasound in the family chat. Everyone sends hearts. A few weeks ago there was nothing visible. {idea}Each stage is the same Hand that will raise you again.{/idea}
old: Growing in the womb is just a natural process.
new: Every stage was shaped by Allah. The same power brings me back.
try: Make dua today for someone expecting a child.

title: From one drop, male and female.
subtitle: The pairs, by His decree
then: Ibn Kathir says man became {idea}either a male or a female by the permission and decree of Allah.{/idea} The same small drop becomes two different kinds of people. {reward}It is all one Creator's work.{/reward}
now: A gender-reveal party: balloons, cake, the whole family filming. Everyone cheers for the surprise. {idea}It was never a surprise to Him.{/idea}
old: What I am was decided by chance.
new: What I am was decreed by Allah, from a single drop.
try: Thank Allah for one thing about how He made you that you usually overlook.

title: Is He not able to bring the dead to life?
subtitle: The question the surah ends on
then: Ibn Kathir: is not He who made {idea}this perfect creation from a weak drop able to repeat it?{/idea} A Companion said that whenever he recited this verse he would say {reward}"Glory to You, of course,"{/reward} and that he heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
now: You reach the end of a surah and close the app. The question hangs there, and you move on. {reward}The Companions answered it out loud.{/reward} The last verse asks you something. Answer.
old: Quran questions are rhetorical. I just read past them.
new: When the Quran asks me something, I can answer it.
try: Next time you recite this verse, say Subhanaka, bala: Glory to You, yes.
